The run and the orchestration graph

Signing starts the run; watching it is optional. The run view appears in the space with the orchestration graph: one node per execution unit, edges for the order the engine derived, colors for live state (grey ready, green running — pulsing, amber parked, blue done, red failed). Click a node for its detail; the log tail runs beneath; Stop aborts every live worker.

How the machine builds

  • Tests first, blind. For each acceptance criterion a probe author writes an executable check — in a detached snapshot of the branch where the implementation-in-progress does not exist. Blinding is structural, not a promise in a prompt. Finished probes persist in a durable store.

  • The coder builds against the brief, with your ask verbatim as the north star and your decisions in force attached. It has a real verify tool: an isolated runner overlays its current work with the held-out probes and returns per-criterion PASS/FAIL with evidence.

  • Green is decided by the oracle, not the worker. A unit completes only when the checks are green for its current state (MANDATORY-GREEN). Not green routes a bounded rework carrying the oracle’s evidence; a unit already green completes without spending a worker at all (grade-first).

  • A supervisor with both sides of the wall audits whether the brief contains every fact the checks require — before the coder spends anything, and again when rounds stall. A disclosure is by definition a contract gap and is recorded in the defect ledger.

  • Containment. A worker that writes outside its declared footprint has the stray paths reverted and the run halts, named.

  • Parallel frontier. Ready units run concurrently (the maxConcurrent setting); slices commit on the branch as they finish.

  • Parked workers. A worker that genuinely needs you parks with a question; answer in the run view and it resumes.

The delivery

The closing gate re-runs every probe from a clean environment, the honesty scan reads the delivered files for self-declared deferrals, and the branch becomes a pull request whose description carries the proofs and every UNDELIVERED line. The machine face — the structured verification trace — persists in the store beside the space.
